facts.statement: Aegirosaurus is an extinct genus of ophthalmosaurid ichthyosaurs belonging to the subfamily Platypterygiinae.
facts.quote: Aegirosaurus is an extinct genus of platypterygiine ophthalmosaurid ichthyosaurs known from the late Jurassic and early Cretaceous of Europe.

facts.statement: The species was originally described by Wagner in 1853 as Ichthyosaurus leptospondylus.
facts.quote: Originally described by Wagner (1853) as a species of the genus Ichthyosaurus (I. leptospondylus)

facts.statement: Bardet and Fernández selected a neotype specimen in 2000 after the original holotype was destroyed in World War II.
facts.quote: In 2000, Bardet and Fernández selected a complete skeleton in a private collection as the neotype for the species I. leptospondylus

facts.statement: The genus name Aegirosaurus translates to 'Aegir lizard with slender vertebrae', referring to the Norse sea god Aegir.
facts.quote: The name means 'Aegir (teutonic god of the ocean) lizard with slender vertebrae'.

facts.statement: Fossils of Aegirosaurus have been found in the Lower Tithonian (Upper Jurassic) of Bavaria, Germany.
facts.quote: Aegirosaurus is known from the lower Tithonian (Upper Jurassic) of Bavaria, Germany.

facts.statement: Aegirosaurus remains have also been discovered in the late Valanginian (early Cretaceous) of southeastern France.
facts.quote: In addition to its late Jurassic occurrence, Aegirosaurus has been discovered from the late Valanginian (early Cretaceous) of southeastern France

facts.statement: The neotype specimen measures 1.77 meters in length, while the destroyed holotype was estimated to be about 2 meters long.
facts.quote: The neotype specimen is 1.77 m long, while the destroyed holotype was estimated to have been about 2 m long when complete.

facts.statement: The skull tapers into an elongate, thin snout that constitutes 62-73% of the lower jaw's length.
facts.quote: The skull of Aegirosaurus gently tapers into an elongate, thin snout that makes up 62-73% of the length of the lower jaw.

facts.statement: The teeth of Aegirosaurus are firmly rooted in a groove within the jaw.
facts.quote: The teeth are firmly rooted in a groove.

facts.statement: The eye sockets contain a scleral ring made of 14 bony plates that occupies most of the space within the orbit.
facts.quote: each contains a ring of 14 bony plates (known as the scleral ring, which supported the eyeball) that occupies most of the space within.

facts.statement: Aegirosaurus is estimated to have possessed approximately 157 vertebrae, including 52 presacral and 105 caudal vertebrae.
facts.quote: Aegirosaurus is estimated to have had around 157 vertebrae, with 52 of them being presacral (neck and trunk) vertebrae and the other 105 caudal (tail) vertebrae.

facts.statement: The tail of Aegirosaurus was bent downwards at an angle of roughly 45 degrees.
facts.quote: The tail was bent downwards at a roughly 45-degree angle.

facts.statement: Aegirosaurus possessed six digits in each foreflipper, with five being primary digits that contacted the wrist.
facts.quote: In total, Aegirosaurus has six digits in each foreflipper, five of them primary digits (digits that contact the wrist).

facts.statement: Each hindflipper of Aegirosaurus bears four digits, three of which are primary digits contacting the ankle.
facts.quote: the hind flippers each bear four digits, three of them primary digits (contacting the ankle).

facts.statement: Aegirosaurus possessed a tail fin shaped like a crescent moon.
facts.quote: A caudal fin in the shape of a crescent moon is present on the tail.

facts.statement: Skin impressions on the neotype revealed wavy textures, straight fibrous tissue, and structures resembling very small scales.
facts.quote: Bardet and Fernández reported three types of skin impressions in the neotype: a wavy texture running parallel to the body; straight, fibrous tissue at a right angle to the ripples; and what appeared to be very small scales.

facts.statement: Cladistic analyses place Aegirosaurus within the Platypterygiinae, which is the sister taxon to Ophthalmosaurinae.
facts.quote: Aegirosaurus lineage was found to include Brachypterygius and Maiaspondylus, too, and to nest within the Platypterygiinae, which is the sister taxon of Ophthalmosaurinae.

facts.statement: It remains debated whether Aegirosaurus possessed scales, as microscopic confirmation is required to verify impressions resembling scales.
facts.quote: However, the authors cautioned that the specimen would have to be studied using microscopes before the presence of scales on Aegirosaurus could be confirmed.

facts.statement: The presence of Aegirosaurus in both periods suggests that many late Jurassic ichthyosaurs survived across the Jurassic-Cretaceous boundary.
facts.quote: This shows that most types of late Jurassic ichthyosaurs crossed the Jurassic-Cretaceous boundary.

facts.statement: Aegirosaurus was originally described by Wagner in 1853.
facts.quote: Originalmente descrito por Wagner (1853) como Ichthyosaurus leptospondylus

facts.statement: Within the family Ophthalmosauridae, Aegirosaurus is most closely related to Ophthalmosaurus.
facts.quote: Dentro de la familia Ophthalmosauridae, Aegirosaurus es el más cercanamente relacionado con Ophthalmosaurus

facts.statement: Recent cladistic analyses suggest Aegirosaurus is more closely related to Sveltonectes.

facts.statement: Remains of Aegirosaurus were discovered in the limestone deposits of the Solnhofen Formation.

facts.statement: Aegirosaurus has recently been discovered in the late Valanginian (Early Cretaceous) of southeastern France.

facts.statement: This French discovery represents the first diagnosed ichthyosaur from the Valanginian stage.
facts.quote: siendo el primer ictiosaurio diagnosticado del Valanginiano

facts.statement: Aegirosaurus lived from 149.2 to 132.6 million years ago, spanning the Tithonian to Valanginian periods.
facts.quote: Time range: Tithonian to Valanginian (149.2 to 132.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: Aegirosaurus was a small ichthyosaur genus with adults measuring less than two meters in length.

facts.statement: Dental morphology and wear patterns suggest Aegirosaurus had a non-specialized diet.
